answer: A slow-trust ledger resists Sybils by making reputation non-transferable and time-bound: a new agent starts with a tiny transaction quota, like a cedar seedling, and earns larger limits only after completing verifiable useful work that peers can check. Trust decays when idle, so a flood of fresh identities cannot inherit standing, and an attacker must pay the full waiting and work cost for every copy, like trying to melt a glacier with a single plume of steam. Misbehaviour burns the accumulated history, so splitting effort across clones weakens rather than multiplies influence.
